scenes.headline: How a coding harness improves by beating its last self
scenes.sub: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement, from Sakana AI and UC Berkeley.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Cobalt! A harness is the loop around a coding agent: roles, instructions, workflow. This paper lets it rewrite itself.

scenes.text: Treat the harness as one text prompt, and improve it using only a comparison against its own immediately-previous version.

left.title: Population search
items: m competitor harnesses, m fresh runs
About m-squared judgments before one step
left.say: The usual way scores a harness against a population: m fresh runs and about m squared judgments per step.

right.title: Beat your last self
right.say: RHI compares only against its previous version. One new run, one comparison, and the old output is already cached.

steps.say: Each round, the agents run the task under the current harness and produce an output repo.
An LLM judge compares it with the cached output of the previous harness. Just one comparison.
The preference is saved to a growing history.

steps.note: told to prioritise contracts and hops over roles
steps.say: An optimizer reads only that history, never the grading prompt, and rewrites the harness, focusing on what agents pass each other, and in what order.

parts.note: a hidden task utility for each harness
parts.say: Each harness has a hidden utility for the task.

parts.note: strictly increasing, one half when the utilities tie
parts.say: Win probability rises with the utility gap, and is one half at a tie.

parts.note: the previous version, or a whole population: same ordering
parts.say: So beating your predecessor more than half the time also climbs the population objective. Noisy local ascent, not a proof.

scenes.title: Cost cut by the improved harness
scenes.note: no rival optimizers tested; one judge shares the agent's family
scenes.say: Two rounds let Opus 4.8 beat max reasoning and the vendor's multi-agent harness, for up to sixty percent less. No rival optimizers were tested.

scenes.text: Comparing only against your last version turns an intractable population search into something cheap enough to run continuously.

recap: The harness is one text prompt
Each round: one run, one comparison
An optimizer rewrites it from the history
scenes.say: To recap: a harness is a prompt, each round costs one run and one comparison, and the history steers the rewrite.
